mean: to have a wildly unrealistic idea
lit: thoughts so strange that one imagines the sky splitting open

use.how: Predicate, often after 是 or 太: 你这个想法太异想天开了。 Also adverbial with 地. Mocks a plan or hope that ignores reality.

near.diff: 杞人忧天 is needless worry about something that will not happen; 异想天开 is an unrealistic hope or plan.
痴心妄想 is harsher and stresses a foolish desire for something one can never get; 异想天开 mocks the idea itself as fantastical.

cue: Your cousin has never cooked a meal, yet plans to open a restaurant next month and be a millionaire by spring. What do you call his plan?

ctx.s: 不复习就想考第一，你别{异想天开}了。
ctx.en: You want to come top without revising? Stop dreaming.

ctx.s: 他想一个月就把英语说得跟母语一样流利，真是{异想天开}。
ctx.en: He wants to speak English as fluently as a native in one month; what a fantasy.

ctx.s: “我打算辞职，靠买彩票养活自己。”“你这也太{异想天开}了吧？”
ctx.en: "I'm going to quit my job and live off lottery tickets." "Isn't that a bit far-fetched?"

ctx.s: 老板{异想天开}地要求我们三天做完一个月的工作。
ctx.en: The boss, with no sense of reality, demanded that we finish a month's work in three days.

ctx.s: 一百年前，很多人觉得人类登上月球是{异想天开}。
ctx.en: A hundred years ago, many people thought humans landing on the moon was a pipe dream.

ctx.s: 这个计划听起来有点{异想天开}，可他还是说服了投资人。
ctx.en: The plan sounded rather fanciful, but he still managed to win over the investors.

bad.s: 他总担心坐飞机会出事，真是{异想天开}。
bad.en: (meant: he always worries the plane will crash, a needless fear)
bad.why: Groundless worry is qǐ rén yōu tiān; this idiom mocks an unrealistic hope or plan, not a fear.

bad.s: 天气预报说明天{异想天开}，会放晴。
bad.en: (meant: the forecast says the sky will clear tomorrow)
bad.why: The opening sky is part of a figure for a fantastical idea; the idiom says nothing about the weather.

mean: to show off one's skill in front of an expert
lit: to swing an axe about at the door of Lu Ban, the master carpenter

story.text: Lu Ban, a craftsman of the state of Lu in the Spring and Autumn period, was so skilled that carpenters came to honour him as the master of their trade. To swing an axe at his door is to show off woodwork in front of the greatest carpenter of all. The Tang writer Liu Zongyuan used the image, saying that to wield an axe at the gate of Ban would take a brazen face.
story.source: 柳宗元《王氏伯仲唱和诗序》

use.how: Most often self-deprecating, before speaking or performing to experts: 我就班门弄斧了。 Also criticises someone who lectures a master.

near.diff: 自以为是 is a general belief that one is always right; 班门弄斧 is a display of skill in front of someone far better at it.

cue: A medical student is asked to say a few words at a conference of senior surgeons and opens with a modest apology. What does she say?

ctx.s: 在您这位书法家面前写字，我真是{班门弄斧}了。
ctx.en: Writing calligraphy in front of a master like you, I'm really showing off before an expert.

ctx.s: 各位都是专家，那我就{班门弄斧}，谈谈自己的一点看法。
ctx.en: You are all experts, so forgive my presumption as I offer a few thoughts of my own.

ctx.s: 他在大厨面前教人怎么切菜，简直是{班门弄斧}。
ctx.en: He was teaching people how to chop vegetables in front of a head chef; talk about showing off before a master.

ctx.s: “你要给钢琴老师弹这首曲子？”“是啊，有点{班门弄斧}，不过是她让我弹的。”
ctx.en: "You're going to play this piece for your piano teacher?" "Yes, it's a bit presumptuous, but she asked me to."

ctx.s: 一个刚学了三个月的新手去纠正教授的发音，这不是{班门弄斧}吗？
ctx.en: A beginner of three months correcting a professor's pronunciation: isn't that showing off before an expert?

ctx.s: 他谦虚地说，在数学系的同事面前讲统计，无异于{班门弄斧}。
ctx.en: He said modestly that talking about statistics in front of colleagues from the maths department was like teaching a master his own trade.

bad.s: 我在一年级小学生面前讲加减法，真是{班门弄斧}。
bad.en: (meant: I was showing off, teaching addition to first-graders)
bad.why: The audience must be experts who know more than the speaker; showing off to beginners is not this idiom.

bad.s: 他是这方面的专家，{班门弄斧}地给我们上了一课。
bad.en: (meant: as an expert, he skilfully taught us a lesson)
bad.why: It never praises an expert's skill; it describes someone lesser displaying skill before a master.

mean: to deceive oneself as well as others
lit: to deceive oneself and deceive others

use.how: Predicate or after 是, takes no object: 这样做是自欺欺人。 Said of pretending an obvious problem is not there.

near.diff: 掩耳盗铃 is a vivid image of hiding from the obvious while doing wrong; 自欺欺人 is the plain statement and is used more widely.
口是心非 is saying one thing while thinking another, deceiving others only; 自欺欺人 means the person is fooling himself too.

cue: A friend hides the unpaid bills in a drawer and tells everyone, himself included, that his shop is doing fine. What is he doing?

ctx.s: 把体重秤藏起来就不胖了吗？别{自欺欺人}了。
ctx.en: Do you think hiding the scales makes you any thinner? Stop kidding yourself.

ctx.s: 公司明明在亏钱，经理却对大家说一切正常，简直是{自欺欺人}。
ctx.en: The company is clearly losing money, yet the manager tells everyone all is well; he's fooling himself as much as us.

ctx.s: “我抄的答案，老师看不出来。”“你这是{自欺欺人}，考试的时候怎么办？”
ctx.en: "I copied the answers; the teacher can't tell." "You're only fooling yourself. What will you do in the exam?"

ctx.s: 他假装没看见那封催款信，用这种{自欺欺人}的办法躲了一个月。
ctx.en: He pretended he hadn't seen the payment reminder, and dodged it for a month by fooling himself like that.

ctx.s: 不去医院检查，就当自己没病，这不是{自欺欺人}吗？
ctx.en: Not getting checked at the hospital and acting as if you're not ill: isn't that just fooling yourself?

ctx.s: 数据造假不过是{自欺欺人}，问题迟早会暴露出来。
ctx.en: Faking the figures only fools yourself along with everyone else; the problem will come out sooner or later.

bad.s: 那个骗子{自欺欺人}，骗走了老人的积蓄。
bad.en: (meant: the swindler cheated the old man out of his savings)
bad.why: A con man who knowingly cheats others is not fooling himself; the idiom needs self-deception about an obvious truth.

bad.s: 他{自欺欺人}了我，说那辆车没出过事故。
bad.en: (meant: he deceived me, saying the car had never been in an accident)
bad.why: It takes no object and is not a verb for deceiving a person; say tā piàn le wǒ.

story.text: Zhao Kuo, son of the Zhao general Zhao She, studied the books of war from youth and argued strategy so well that even his father could not beat him in debate, yet Zhao She did not trust him with an army, saying he spoke of war too lightly. Later, at the battle of Changping against Qin, the king of Zhao replaced the veteran general Lian Po with Zhao Kuo. He changed the existing plans, was surrounded by the Qin army and killed, and the Zhao army was lost.

use.how: Predicate or after 是 / 只是: 这些计划不过是纸上谈兵。 Criticises talk, plans or knowledge never tested in practice.

near.diff: 一知半解 is knowing only part of something; 纸上谈兵 may know the theory well but has never put it into practice.

cue: A new manager has read every leadership book but has never run a team, and his detailed plan falls apart on the first day.

ctx.s: 他自己从没开过车，却总教别人怎么开，真是{纸上谈兵}。
ctx.en: He has never driven himself, yet he's always telling others how to drive; it's all theory.

ctx.s: 只读管理书、不去公司实习，学到的东西不过是{纸上谈兵}。
ctx.en: If you only read management books and never do an internship, what you learn is just theory.

ctx.s: “你的方案看起来不错，试过吗？”“还没有。”“那还只是{纸上谈兵}。”
ctx.en: "Your plan looks good; have you tried it?" "Not yet." "Then it's still just theory."

ctx.s: 计划写得再漂亮，不到现场看看，也是{纸上谈兵}。
ctx.en: However fine the plan looks, if you never visit the site it's just armchair strategy.

ctx.s: 不少球迷在网上{纸上谈兵}，好像比教练还懂战术。
ctx.en: Plenty of fans play armchair general online, as if they understood tactics better than the coach.

ctx.s: 我们不能满足于{纸上谈兵}，必须尽快把想法拿到市场上检验。
ctx.en: We can't be content with theorising; we have to test our ideas in the market as soon as possible.

bad.s: 这位老将军打了几十年仗，最会{纸上谈兵}。
bad.en: (meant: this old general fought for decades and is a master of strategy)
bad.why: It criticises theory with no experience; it cannot praise someone whose skill comes from long practice.

bad.s: 他拿出笔在纸上{纸上谈兵}，写了一篇作文。
bad.en: (meant: he took out a pen and wrote an essay on paper)
bad.why: The paper is figurative; the idiom is not a description of writing or of discussing anything on paper.

lit: not understanding, yet pretending to understand

use.how: Predicate, often in advice or warnings: 不懂就问，别不懂装懂。 Said of hiding one's ignorance instead of asking.

near.diff: 一知半解 is honestly knowing only a little; 不懂装懂 is knowingly pretending to understand what one does not.
自以为是 is sincerely believing oneself right; 不懂装懂 knows it does not understand and hides it.

cue: In a meeting full of jargon, a new intern nods at everything, then cannot do the task because he never asked what any of it meant.

ctx.s: 不明白就问老师，别{不懂装懂}。
ctx.en: If you don't understand, ask the teacher; don't pretend you do.

ctx.s: 他明明听不懂，却一直点头，{不懂装懂}。
ctx.en: He clearly couldn't follow, yet kept nodding, pretending he understood.

ctx.s: “这个词你认识吗？”“认识……其实不认识。”“不认识就说嘛，{不懂装懂}有什么用？”
ctx.en: "Do you know this word?" "Yes... actually, no." "Then say so. What's the use of pretending?"

ctx.s: 医生最怕病人{不懂装懂}，自己乱吃药。
ctx.en: What doctors dread most is patients who pretend to know and take medicine on their own.

ctx.s: 刚来公司的时候，我{不懂装懂}，结果把客户的订单弄错了。
ctx.en: When I first joined the company I pretended to understand, and ended up getting a customer's order wrong.

ctx.s: 承认自己不知道并不丢人，{不懂装懂}才让人看不起。
ctx.en: There's no shame in admitting you don't know; it's pretending to know that people look down on.

bad.s: 老师问谁打破了窗户，他{不懂装懂}，说什么都不知道。
bad.en: (meant: asked who broke the window, he played dumb and said he knew nothing)
bad.why: That is the opposite, pretending not to know (zhuāng hú tu); this idiom is pretending to understand.

bad.s: 这道数学题太难了，我完全{不懂装懂}。
bad.en: (meant: this maths problem is too hard; I don't understand it at all)
bad.why: It needs pretence; simply not understanding anything is yī qiào bù tōng.

lit: to hold on firmly and never slacken

use.how: Predicate, adverbial with 地, or attribute of 的努力: 坚持不懈地练习。 Praises long, steady effort toward a worthwhile goal.

near.diff: 半途而废 is the opposite: giving up halfway.
再接再厉 urges more effort after a success; 坚持不懈 is steady effort kept up over a long time, success or not.

cue: For six years a woman studies every night after work, fails the bar exam three times and finally passes on the fourth try.

ctx.s: 只要{坚持不懈}，你的中文一定会进步。
ctx.en: As long as you keep at it, your Chinese will definitely improve.

ctx.s: 他每天早上跑步，{坚持不懈}，身体越来越好。
ctx.en: He runs every morning without fail, and his health keeps getting better.

ctx.s: “我已经失败好几次了。”“别灰心，{坚持不懈}才能成功。”
ctx.en: "I've already failed several times." "Don't lose heart; only steady perseverance brings success."

ctx.s: 经过十年{坚持不懈}的努力，她终于开了自己的诊所。
ctx.en: After ten years of unrelenting effort, she finally opened her own clinic.

ctx.s: 科学家们{坚持不懈}地研究，终于找到了新的治疗方法。
ctx.en: The scientists kept up their research tirelessly and finally found a new treatment.

ctx.s: 这位老人几十年来{坚持不懈}地在山上种树，把荒山变成了森林。
ctx.en: For decades this old man planted trees on the hill without letting up, turning the barren slopes into forest.

bad.s: 他{坚持不懈}要我请他吃饭，我只好答应了。
bad.en: (meant: he insisted that I buy him dinner, so I agreed)
bad.why: On its own jiānchí can mean to insist on a demand; this idiom only means persevering at a long effort.

bad.s: 他{坚持不懈}地喝完了一杯水。
bad.en: (meant: he drank up a glass of water)
bad.why: It needs a long, sustained effort over time, not one short ordinary action.

mean: to keep up the good work and do even better
lit: to clash again and sharpen again, like a fighting cock

story.text: The phrase comes from a linked poem about cockfighting written together by the Tang poets Han Yu and Meng Jiao. Describing the birds, it says they clash, sharpen their beaks and go back in again. jiē was the clash and lì (first written with the character for a whetstone) the sharpening; the fighter that returns ever keener became a call to build on success and push on.

use.how: Encouragement after a good result, often from teachers, coaches or leaders: 希望你再接再厉。 Takes no object.

near.diff: 坚持不懈 is steady effort over a long time; 再接再厉 builds on a success just achieved.
精益求精 is refining something already good to make it finer; 再接再厉 is pushing on to the next achievement.

cue: Your team has just won the regional final, and before the national round the coach tells them to keep it up and aim even higher. What does she say?

ctx.s: “老师，我这次进了前十名！”“太棒了，{再接再厉}！”
ctx.en: "Teacher, I made the top ten this time!" "Brilliant, keep it up!"

ctx.s: 你这次考得很好，希望你{再接再厉}。
ctx.en: You did very well in this exam; I hope you'll keep up the good work.

ctx.s: 比赛赢了，教练对队员说：“大家{再接再厉}，争取拿冠军！”
ctx.en: After the win the coach told the players: "Keep it up, everyone, let's go for the title!"

ctx.s: 去年的销售成绩不错，今年我们要{再接再厉}。
ctx.en: Last year's sales were good; this year we need to build on that and do even better.

ctx.s: 领导在会上表扬了我们组，并鼓励大家{再接再厉}。
ctx.en: At the meeting the boss praised our team and encouraged us to keep up the good work.

ctx.s: 首战告捷后，球队{再接再厉}，又连赢了三场。
ctx.en: After winning their opening game, the team kept the momentum going and won three more in a row.

bad.s: 你这次考试作弊被发现了，下次要{再接再厉}。
bad.en: (meant: you were caught cheating; do better next time)
bad.why: It urges someone to build on good work; said after wrongdoing it sounds like encouraging more of it.

bad.s: 他{再接再厉}了自己的工作，升了职。
bad.en: (meant: he kept improving at his job and was promoted)
bad.why: It takes no object and no le like this; say tā zài gōngzuò shang zài jiē zài lì.

mean: to do one's best (without promising success)
lit: to act with all the strength one has

use.how: Predicate, often 我会尽力而为 or 尽力而为就好. A modest promise or reassurance that leaves room for failure.

near.diff: 全力以赴 is an all-out, determined push; 尽力而为 promises effort but quietly admits the result is uncertain.

cue: A friend asks if you can get them a ticket to a sold-out concert. You'll try, but you can't promise anything. What do you reply?

ctx.s: 考试别太紧张，{尽力而为}就好。
ctx.en: Don't get too nervous about the exam; just do your best.

ctx.s: 这件事我不能保证成功，但我会{尽力而为}。
ctx.en: I can't guarantee this will work, but I'll do what I can.

ctx.s: “你能帮我找到那本书吗？”“我{尽力而为}吧，不一定找得到。”
ctx.en: "Can you find that book for me?" "I'll do my best, but I may not find it."

ctx.s: 医生对家属说：“我们会{尽力而为}，但你们也要做好心理准备。”
ctx.en: The doctor told the family: "We will do everything we can, but you should prepare yourselves."

ctx.s: 时间这么紧，老板也只要求大家{尽力而为}，不强求完美。
ctx.en: With time this tight, the boss only asked everyone to do their best, not to be perfect.

ctx.s: 比赛结果谁也说不准，每个人{尽力而为}，问心无愧就行。
ctx.en: Nobody can predict the result; if everyone does their best, we'll have nothing to regret.

bad.s: 为了拿冠军，我们要{尽力而为}，不惜一切代价！
bad.en: (meant: we'll go all out to win the title, whatever it costs)
bad.why: It is a modest hedge; an all-out, whatever-it-takes vow calls for quán lì yǐ fù.

bad.s: 他每天都{尽力而为}这份工作。
bad.en: (meant: every day he does his best at this job)
bad.why: It takes no object; say tā jìnlì zuò hǎo zhè fèn gōngzuò instead.

lit: to follow the proper order and advance gradually

use.how: Predicate, adverbial with 地, or after 是…的: 学习要循序渐进。 Said of learning, training or reform that moves in stages.

near.diff: 拔苗助长 is the opposite mistake: forcing quick progress and spoiling it.
脚踏实地 is a down-to-earth, practical attitude; 循序渐进 is the gradual order in which progress is made.

cue: A beginner wants to run a marathon next month, but his coach has him start with short jogs and add a little distance each week.

ctx.s: 学外语要{循序渐进}，不能着急。
ctx.en: Learning a foreign language has to go step by step; you can't rush it.

ctx.s: 刚开始健身，运动量应该{循序渐进}地增加。
ctx.en: When you start working out, you should increase the load gradually.

ctx.s: “我能直接学最难的课吗？”“最好还是{循序渐进}，先把基础打好。”
ctx.en: "Can I go straight to the hardest course?" "Better to take it step by step and get the basics right first."

ctx.s: 这本教材从简单到复杂，编排得{循序渐进}。
ctx.en: This textbook moves from easy to hard; it is arranged in a careful progression.

ctx.s: 公司的改革是{循序渐进}的，不会一下子改变所有制度。
ctx.en: The company's reforms are gradual; they won't change every rule at once.

ctx.s: 他想一个月减十公斤，医生劝他减肥也要{循序渐进}。
ctx.en: He wanted to lose ten kilos in a month; the doctor advised him that weight loss too should be gradual.

bad.s: 他学了半年钢琴，进步飞快，真是{循序渐进}。
bad.en: (meant: after half a year of piano he has improved by leaps and bounds)
bad.why: It means slow, orderly progress; rapid leaps are tū fēi měng jìn.

bad.s: 我们在车站{循序渐进}地排队买票。
bad.en: (meant: we queued in order at the station to buy tickets)
bad.why: It is about gradual progress in learning or development, not waiting one's turn in a line (that is àn shùnxù).

mean: able to endure hardship and hard work
lit: to eat bitterness and bear toil

use.how: Describes a person's lasting character, as predicate or in 吃苦耐劳的精神: 他很吃苦耐劳。 Common in references and job adverts.

near.diff: 坚持不懈 is persistence toward one goal; 吃苦耐劳 is a character that bears hard conditions and heavy work without complaint.
千辛万苦 names the hardships themselves; 吃苦耐劳 describes the person able to bear them.

cue: A recruiter describes a candidate who grew up on a farm, works long shifts without complaint and never shirks the dirty jobs.

ctx.s: 这个小伙子{吃苦耐劳}，老板很喜欢他。
ctx.en: This young man is hard-working and tough, and the boss likes him a lot.

ctx.s: 我爷爷年轻时很{吃苦耐劳}，什么活都干过。
ctx.en: When my grandfather was young he could take any hardship; he did every kind of work.

ctx.s: 招聘广告上写着：要求{吃苦耐劳}，能适应经常出差。
ctx.en: The job advert says: must be hard-working, able to cope with frequent travel.

ctx.s: “你觉得自己最大的优点是什么？”“我比较{吃苦耐劳}。”
ctx.en: "What do you think is your greatest strength?" "I'm quite hard-working and don't mind tough conditions."

ctx.s: 靠着{吃苦耐劳}的精神，这家人从一个小摊做成了一家大饭店。
ctx.en: Through sheer hard work and endurance, the family grew a small stall into a big restaurant.

ctx.s: 山区的农民世世代代{吃苦耐劳}，在石头缝里种出了庄稼。
ctx.en: For generations the mountain farmers have toiled through hardship, growing crops in the cracks between rocks.

bad.s: 这道菜太辣了，我{吃苦耐劳}地吃完了。
bad.en: (meant: the dish was too spicy, but I bravely finished it)
bad.why: Its bitterness is figurative hardship; the idiom is a character trait, not putting up with food or one unpleasant moment.

bad.s: 他今天{吃苦耐劳}了八个小时。
bad.en: (meant: he worked hard for eight hours today)
bad.why: It describes a lasting quality of a person and cannot take le and a length of time; say tā jīntiān xīnkǔ gàn le bā gè xiǎoshí.
